humanities_role_explanation: Items are paintings of Christian saints labelled with Iconclass codes; the task is iconographic classification, a disciplinary competence in art history, not a generic vision test.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Painting images are paired with textual prompts listing class labels or Iconclass descriptions; few-shot adds labelled exemplar images. The CSV metadata lists text only, but the images are the stimuli.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Single-label classification of Christian saints in paintings (iconography classification with Iconclass codes), identifying the saint from visual attributes; zero-shot with labels, with Iconclass descriptions, and few-shot with five exemplars.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to single-label classification of Christian saints in three datasets.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash, plus CLIP and SigLIP variants.

summary: The paper benchmarks CLIP, SigLIP, GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 models on single-label classification of Christian saints across ArtDL, an Iconclass AI Test Set subset and a Wikidata subset. It compares labels only, Iconclass descriptions and few-shot exemplars against fine-tuned ResNet50 baselines. Multimodal LLMs beat the baselines on ArtDL and ICONCLASS but not on Wikidata.
key_findings: Gemini-2.5 Pro reached 90.45% on ArtDL, beating the ResNet50 baseline at 84.44%. On Wikidata, SigLIP-so400m was best at 66.29% while the LLMs were around 45%. Descriptions generally helped zero-shot, and few-shot mostly lowered accuracy. Cross-dataset consistency was lower for LLMs than for contrastive models.
gold_upstream: ArtDL (Milani and Fraternali) and the Iconclass AI Test Set (Posthumus); Iconclass codes from Wikidata. Annotation production not described in this paper.
facets_explanation: Labels are the Iconclass codes already attached to images in ArtDL, the ICONCLASS AI Test Set and Wikidata, filtered to single-saint images among the top ten classes. The paper does not say how these annotations were produced. Identifying the saint requires iconographic knowledge not in the image itself.
results_explanation: Table 2 gives gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06 90.45% on ArtDL Test 1, the headline. The largest input gap is siglip-large-patch16-384 on ArtDL, 54.45% (labels) vs 72.21% (descriptions), roughly 18 points, but clip-vit-large-patch14 on ArtDL goes 30.58% to 44.31% (about 14); the largest I found is siglip-base-patch16-512 on Wikidata, 57.47% vs 46.94%, and the 28-point figure is not directly supported and should be re-checked. No human baseline is reported. Dataset size is 1,864 + 863 + 718 = 3,445 images.

dataset_size.quote: resulting in a dataset comprising 863 images

evaluation_set_size.quote: The test set, published along with the paper, contains 1,864 images.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: Models were tested under three conditions: (1) classification using class labels, (2) classification with Iconclass descriptions, and (3) few-shot learning with five exemplars.

gold_source.quote: We investigated the images belonging to three collections, which we selected for their native support of Iconclass classes.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: This configuration tests the model’s ability to leverage pre-trained knowledge connections between visual features and semantic concepts.

answer_multiplicity.quote: Each is mapped to a single iconographic label

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: Test 2 is a zero-shot classification task with label descriptions.
